例句

  • A recent survey shows that the younger generation is reducing its alcohol consumption.（最近一项调查显示，年轻一代在减少饮酒量。）
  • Social media has a strong influence on our lifestyle and diet.（社交媒体对我们的生活方式和饮食影响很大。）
  • Doctors encourage people to drink in moderate amounts because too much alcohol is harmful to both physical and mental health.（医生鼓励人们适量饮酒，因为喝太多对身心都有害。）
  • It is hard to convince someone to change a bad habit.（很难说服一个人改掉坏习惯。）

过关标准：遮住中文看英文，能说出 22 个以上的意思，再挑 5 个自己造句（最好跟健康、生活习惯有关，雅思口语常考）。

BBC 6 Minute English：Are people drinking less alcohol?（10 月 8 日）。音频和原文都已经放在页面里，不用打开 BBC 网站。

  1. 先把上面的听前生词过一遍。听不太懂的话，可以先点开下面的原文读懂再听。
  2. 第一遍不看文字，只听大意，回答开头的问题：很多英国人一月份整月戒酒，这个挑战叫什么？a) No-drink New Year b) Alcohol-free January c) Dry January
  3. 第二遍点开下面的原文精听，听不出的地方暂停、倒回去并标出来。
  4. 第三遍挑 Daniel 那段（讲自己为什么戒酒）跟读，模仿语调和连读。
  5. 记住 6 个表达：sober（不喝酒的）、societal pressure（社会压力）、the norm（常态）、self-optimisation content（自我提升类内容）、tout（大力宣扬）、pushback（反对，反弹）。
点开看原文（难词带中文，点虚线词显示）

Georgie：Hi Neil.

Neil：Hi Georgie. Do you want to hear something quite unusual for me?

Georgie：Err, yes!

Neil：I haven't had an alcoholic含酒精的 drink this year.

Georgie：Wow! That is really impressive令人佩服的. How do you feel? Like a new person?

Neil：I do feel very good, I have to say.

Georgie：I can't say the same – I did have a few alcoholic含酒精的 drinks at the weekend with my friends. But in many parts of the world, people don't drink alcohol at all. In the UK it's very common – that is until recently. Today on 6 Minute English, we're going to find out why many people are choosing to give up戒掉；放弃 or cut down on减少（某物的量） alcohol, and we'll be asking, Is this the end of British drinking culture饮酒文化? OK. Neil, let's start with a quiz question. Many people in the UK and other countries choose to give up戒掉；放弃 alcohol in the new year for the whole of the month of January, but what is the challenge called? Is it:

a) No-drink New Year

b) Alcohol-free January, or

c) Dry January?

Neil：Well, I know the answer to this, but I'm not going to give it away说漏答案.

Georgie：OK. Well, then our listeners can find out the answer at the end of the programme.

Neil：Yes, they can. So, Georgie, I hear all the time that younger people don't drink as much alcohol today as they used to in the past. Is that true?

Georgie：Well, in the UK, surveys suggest that 16 to 24-year-olds are more likely to be non-drinkers than the older generations.

Neil：OK. So, why are more young people choosing to be sober不喝酒的；清醒的? That means not to drink alcohol.

Georgie：Well, the BBC World Service podcast What in the World have been investigating this. Presenter Hannah Gelbart met three young people who choose to be sober不喝酒的；清醒的 for some alcohol-free drinks to find out more. Here's Daniel's story:

Daniel：Yeah. So, today I don't drink at all, but when I was in my early 20s, I think I felt maybe a bit of, like, societal社会的 pressure – you know, work drinks or being at uni, where it was the norm常态；惯例 to just join in参与进去. I think you'd probably get a few weird glances瞥一眼 if you're like, "Yeah, I'm not going to join in参与进去 at all." So, I did that and I think Covid lockdown封控；封城 just gave me a bit of confidence to say, "OK, let me step away from远离；退出 this. It's not necessarily something I want to do moving forward今后，往后."

Hannah Gelbart：So, how many years have you been sober不喝酒的；清醒的 for?

Daniel：I would say it's been six years now.

Hannah Gelbart：Six years?

Georgie：So, Daniel says that when he was younger, he felt societal社会的 pressure to drink alcohol. Societal社会的 pressure is feeling like you need to do something because lots of people around you are doing it.

Neil：Right. So, Daniel says drinking was the norm常态；惯例 at university and after work. The norm常态；惯例 is a way of saying that something is normal or common.

Georgie：But during the Covid-19 pandemic大流行病, when people in the UK were unable to socialise社交（英式也拼 socialise） and visit pubs and bars, Daniel's attitude to alcohol changed. After that, he decided to be sober不喝酒的；清醒的 and he hasn't had a drink for about six years.

Neil：So, Georgie, it seems like many young people don't drink at all and lots of them share their experience of being sober不喝酒的；清醒的 on social media. But recently there's been a bit of a change, hasn't there?

Georgie：Yes. Whilst many people use social media to share their experience of drinking less alcohol or no alcohol at all, some people have been saying that they want to go out more and drink and have fun with friends. They argue we're too worried about fitness and wellness身心健康, and that drinking some alcohol to have a good time is fine. Here's Millie talking more about this to BBC World Service podcast What in the World:

Millie：I think we had this, like, rise of self-optimisation content自我提升类内容. I think unfortunately sobriety不喝酒；清醒, kind of, got swept in with被一并卷进 that and it got touted大肆宣扬 as this way to, you know, get up at 5am, do a HYROX. And, you know, for many of us, that's probably not our reality with not drinking. It's that we do it to feel a bit more sane精神正常的；理智的 or, you know, things like that. And so, I think now we are entering this, like, almost pushback反对；反弹 era of that content and you're seeing celebrities名人，明星... Like, it's not just alcohol – you're seeing more celebrities名人，明星 smoking and, like, posting that on their Instagram and not worrying if it's brand-friendly符合品牌形象的.

Neil：OK. So, Millie thinks that being sober不喝酒的；清醒的 is associated有关联的 with certain kinds of self-optimisation content自我提升类内容, where people talk about fitness, diet and having big goals for themselves.

Georgie：Yes, and Millie says being sober不喝酒的；清醒的 gets touted大肆宣扬 as a way to get up at 5am to exercise. In other words, people talk about it a lot and try to encourage people to do it.

Neil：But Millie says that being sober不喝酒的；清醒的 isn't always about being super fit and healthy. For her, it's about being sane精神正常的；理智的.

Georgie：But still, Millie thinks there's a pushback反对；反弹 against self-optimisation content自我提升类内容. Pushback反对；反弹 means a criticism批评 of the content, and people are pushing back反对；对着干 by doing the opposite. For example, lots of celebrities名人，明星 post about themselves drinking and smoking.

Neil：Well, Georgie, I've decided to try to give up戒掉；放弃 alcohol for a whole year, but I don't think everybody should do that if they don't want to. It's really up to the individual由个人决定.

Georgie：Yeah, I still enjoy having a few drinks with my friends. I think it's just all about balance关键在于平衡, really. OK. Neil, it's time to reveal揭晓；透露 the answer to this week's question. I asked, "What was the name given for when people give up戒掉；放弃 alcohol in January?"

Neil：Yes. And the answer is Dry January.

Georgie：That is correct. Well done! Let's recap回顾；总结 the vocabulary we learned in this programme, starting with sober不喝酒的；清醒的, which describes someone who doesn't drink alcohol or take recreational娱乐性的；消遣的 drugs.

Neil：Societal社会的 pressure is the feeling that you should do something because lots of other people expect you to.

Georgie：Saying something is the norm常态；惯例 is a way to say it's usual or common.

Neil：Self-optimisation content自我提升类内容 means videos and posts about being fit, healthy and achieving big goals.

Georgie：If somebody touts大肆宣扬 an idea or lifestyle, they talk about it a lot and try to convince说服 people to do it.

Neil：And pushback反对；反弹 is strong criticism批评 of a trend, and people doing the opposite.

Georgie：Once again, our six minutes are up, but don't forget to test what you've learned with the worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

Neil：Thank you for joining us and goodbye.

Georgie：Goodbye!

过关标准：不看原文能用中文说出这集讲了什么（年轻人为什么少喝酒，现在又出现了什么反弹），6 个表达都知道意思，Daniel 那段能流利读下来。

小练习

  1. In some countries, working late every day is ______ ______.（两个词，很常见的事）
  2. He has been ______ for two years and doesn't miss alcohol at all.
  3. The government wants to ______ the amount of sugar children eat.
  4. Many teenagers start smoking because of ______ ______.（两个词，社会压力）
  5. The new rule faced strong ______ from local businesses.
点开看答案

开头那题选 c，Dry January。填空：1. the norm 2. sober 3. reduce 4. societal pressure（peer pressure 也行）5. pushback（criticism 也行）
